findings.atomic_item: sub_question 13 ('What are the top 5 real failure modes (example, expected vs actual, root cause, mitigation, implemented or not)?') + required_format 'failure-mode table with real-example slots' + assignment deliverable 'top 5 failure modes with real examples'
findings.issue: Section 8 gives five prose paragraphs (contamination, identifier hallucination, sarcasm/multi-intent, verbosity, staleness) with cause + mitigation, but no table, no per-mode example / expected-vs-actual pair, and no implemented-or-not flag. Examples are explicitly deferred as NOT MEASURED until labelling. The assignment deliverable requires real examples; a re-engineering plan still owes a table shell with slots.
findings.location: ## 8. Failure Modes Headline-Number Critique and Limits — five paragraphs starting 'First, same-thread contamination...'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace/append the five paragraphs with (or with a lead-in to) a 5-row table with columns: # | Failure mode | Concrete example slot (thread-id + quote placeholder, marked NOT MEASURED) | Expected vs actual | Root cause | Mitigation | Implemented? Add one row per existing shape; keep prose as table notes. Do not fabricate examples — use empty slots with stratum labels (e.g., identifier-heavy, sarcasm).

findings.issue: Section 4 decision table uses columns Decision/Chosen/Rejected/Evidence only. Cost, latency, and risk live in surrounding prose ($42 vs $740, 56x faster, <30ms, 100-200ms rerank, ops ledger) but are not columnar, so the reviewer cannot scan tradeoffs per decision as the decomposition requires.
findings.location: ## 4. System Architecture — table '| Decision | Chosen | Rejected | Evidence |'
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the table to '| Decision (purpose) | Chosen | Rejected alternatives | Evidence | Cost | Latency | Risk/failure if wrong |' and backfill each row from existing prose (ETL, graded store, scale-up, framework, harness, backbone, judge). Mark unmeasured cells NOT MEASURED rather than dropping the columns.

findings.atomic_item: required_format 'ranked architecture comparison with committed recommendation'
findings.issue: Section 4 commits to a plain dependency-ordered pipeline (SetFit-first, gated hybrid, caged judge, MaxProb floor) and Section 2 ranks brands, but there is no ranked comparison of system architectures (e.g., rank 1/2/3 with when-each-wins). The reader gets a verdict plus a per-decision table, not an ordered comparison the format demands.
findings.location: ## 4. System Architecture — Minimal Design That Maximizes Trust per Complexity
findings.suggested_fix: Add a compact ranked list/table before the decision table: e.g., (1) plain pipeline [committed], (2) retrieval-filtered LLM-first fallback, (3) graph-orchestrated agent [rejected] — with one-line when-it-wins and reversal condition per rank, reusing existing reversal language (router AUGRC fail, 5-point identifier gate, genuine retrieve-grade-retry loop).

findings.atomic_item: sub_question 7 ('What do trivial and simple baselines score, and why are they honest rather than strawmen?') + assignment deliverable 'results vs at least two baselines (one trivial, one simple)'
findings.issue: Section 7 correctly defines trivial (majority/fixed/always-escalate) and simple (TF-IDF/BM25 neighbor + direct-LLM + raw threshold) plus the honesty criterion (6-8pt MDE at n=200), but reports no scores — all NOT MEASURED until rebuild. Deferral honors the no-fabrication scope condition, yet the atomic item asks what they score, so the report needs an explicit empty results shell rather than prose-only deferral.
findings.location: ## 7. Evaluation Baselines and the LLM Judge — 'Scores are NOT MEASURED until rebuild'
findings.suggested_fix: Insert a baseline results table shell (rows: trivial, simple, full system; columns: intent macro-F1, retrieval R@10, groundedness, auto-handle risk@coverage, with 95% intervals) with every cell NOT MEASURED + footnote that complexity ships only on >MDE gain. No numbers invented; structure only.

findings.atomic_item: sub_question 12 ('What is the LLM-as-judge rubric, and how well does it agree with humans — why should the judge be trusted?')
findings.issue: Rubric is fully specified (caged pointwise, 3x1-5 dimensions + categorical escalate verdict, debias bundle) and promotion gates are quantified (weighted ~0.60, escalation ~0.65, raw >=75%, swap >=0.80, jackknife intervals), but no measured agreement exists — correctly, per no-fabrication — and there is no results/agreement table shell or disagreement-analysis placeholder, so 'how much' is answered as a threshold, not as evidence with a slot for it.
findings.location: ## 7. Evaluation Baselines and the LLM Judge — judge gates paragraph
findings.suggested_fix: Add an agreement-results table shell (per-dimension weighted agreement, escalation agreement/F1, raw agreement, swap consistency, length/self-preference gaps — all NOT MEASURED) plus a 2-3 sentence disagreement-analysis placeholder (20-30 mismatch critiques feeding anchors) so step-14 patcher has hunks to fill post-study.

findings.atomic_item: sub_question 1 ('What does good mean for the selected brand, and what was deliberately NOT built?')
findings.issue: Section 1 lists exclusions (multi-brand, live channel, tool loops, learned sparse, dynamic fusion, fine-tuning, streaming eval, full-3M claims) and promises 'each carries a revival condition below,' but revival conditions are scattered across later sections (framework revisit, hybrid demotion, LLM-first reversal, calibrator admission) and never itemized against the exclusion list, forcing the reader to reconstruct the mapping.
findings.location: ## 1. Problem Framing — 'Deliberately not built' paragraph ending 'each carries a revival condition below'
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the NOT-built list a parenthetical revival condition per bullet (e.g., 'learned sparse — revisit only if tuned hybrid fails 5-point identifier gate and document-only latency proven'), reusing conditions already stated in Sections 4-6. No new content; collect existing conditions into the list.
